listenings.text: Hello, I'm Hannah, and I write film reviews for a magazine in London. People often ask me about my favorite scene in a period drama. It's a dinner scene. A big family was having dinner in their country house. It was raining outside, and the candles were burning on the table. Everybody was talking and laughing. Then, while the father was telling a story, a servant came in with a letter. The father read it, and his face changed. Nobody said a word. The plot of the whole series changes in that moment. And no, I won't tell you what the letter said. No spoilers!

Hi, I'm Mike. I never liked period dramas. Then, two years ago, I was flying from New York to London at night. Everybody was sleeping, but I couldn't sleep. I was looking for a film, and I chose a period drama because it was the longest one. Big mistake, I thought. But after twenty minutes, I was crying. The main character was a young woman in the 1800s, and she was fighting for the right to study. While I was watching the last scene, the plane landed. The woman next to me said: you were crying, sir. I said: it's the costumes. They're beautiful.

paras: Big houses, long dresses, letters written by hand: period dramas take us to another time. Millions of people watch them, and many of them do not even like history classes. So why do we love them? One reason is the costumes. Designers work for months on every dress, and in some films the costumes are almost a main character.

Another reason is the plot. Most period dramas are about families, love and secrets, and those things never change. In the film Pride and Prejudice, set in England more than two hundred years ago, Elizabeth was walking alone in the fields early one morning when Mr. Darcy appeared. Nobody says much in that scene, but everybody remembers it.

Series like Downton Abbey and The Crown made the genre even more popular. While audiences were watching the stories of a rich family or a young queen, they were also learning a little history. A good review can help you choose your next period drama, but be careful: some reviews have spoilers.
